assumptions.summary: One representative vehicle mode stands for each of CV, EV, and HEV.
France, USA, and China stand for European, American, and Asian countries.
Vehicle performance remains unchanged over the 50-year horizon.
Every vehicle travels 10000 km per year.
Every unspecified power plant produces 10000000 kWh annually on average.
Population density and road capacity justify logistic total-fleet growth.
Government targets a 90% reduction in current vehicle oil consumption by 2055.
EV/HEV begins at 5% of total vehicles and EV:HEV reaches 3.
HEV uses one ninth of annual travel in electric-only mode.
Off-peak energy is 27.3% of annual generation across all countries and years.
Thermal power can be reduced to 10% while source costs and capacities remain as listed.
Grid CO2 intensity and vehicle consumption adequately proxy fossil-fuel reliance.
A fixed nitrogen-to-CO2 ratio adequately proxies health impact.

independent_extensions.summary: Fit country fleet models with sourced data, time-varying ceilings, residual diagnostics, uncertainty, and held-out years.
Rebuild vehicle allocation as a unit-consistent constrained optimization with defined objectives and policy authority.
Use hourly regional load, charging behavior, storage, losses, transmission, and nonnegative residual constraints.
Normalize cost/capacity units and solve a reliability-aware multi-period generation expansion model.
Replace the average plant with type-, scale-, location-, lead-time-, lifetime-, and dispatch-specific infrastructure.
Use lifecycle vehicle and grid emissions with time-varying marginal generation and battery supply chains.
Define all-CV counterfactual coefficients and derive country/world weights from a documented coverage design.

Use discounted social cost-benefit accounting with taxes, transfers, opportunity costs, and double-counting controls.
Replace nitrogen with pollutant-specific emissions, exposure, dose-response, morbidity, mortality, and uncertainty.
Backtest each country model and propagate all uncertainties to decision-stability and non-use conditions.

language_observations.summary: Human style is carried by explicit scope, handoffs, proxy disclosure, failed-forecast replacement, adverse-result retention, metric switches, and actor-owned conclusions rather than connector density.
scope narrows pressure into a counterfactual: Convert a global pressure into a bounded horizon, representative places, and paired scenarios before calculating.
roadmap names sequential model handoffs: State the quantity model, the supply model, and the impact model in order, with each output feeding the next.
representative proxies are declared: Choose one observable proxy for each class and state why it stands in for the broader population.
resource-limited growth motivates logistic form: Map bounded population or road capacity to a logistic analogy, then fit historical totals before allocating types.
unknown exhaustion is replaced by an explicit target: Admit that an exact reserve date cannot be known, then replace it with a stated reduction target and horizon.
total growth is separated from type allocation: Solve total fleet growth first, allocate CV/EV/HEV second, and pass the fleet counts into energy and impact models.
actor goals become constrained optimization: Translate environment, society, business, and individual goals into an objective with explicit lower and upper bounds.
a temporal surplus becomes a charging resource: Read the daily load shape, quantify off-peak energy, and subtract it from vehicle demand before adding generation.
unresolved heterogeneity is degraded to an average plant: State that plant types and scales cannot be enumerated, replace them with an average output, and expose the resulting planning approximation.
an adverse transition is retained and explained: Keep a temporary emissions increase, identify the competing fleet and grid mechanisms, then continue to the later decline.
a disputed upstream effect is tested by system boundary: Move from tailpipe claims to grid-weighted CO2 intensity and compare mixed fleets against an all-conventional counterfactual.
insufficient environmental benefit triggers feasibility metrics: Acknowledge that environmental benefit alone may not secure adoption, then switch to cost, jobs, investment, and health proxies.
one model output is reused downstream: Carry fleet counts, vacancy, plant counts, or job counts into the next equation, table, or decision without changing their type.
heterogeneous benefits share a money scale: Convert jobs and driving savings into salary and operating savings before comparing them with investment.
three-country proxies are weighted into a world result: Combine country-specific curves with explicit weights, then state the scope and proxy limits of the global conclusion.
recommendations are split by actor: Separate government responsibilities from individual and manufacturer levers, then trace each to a model output.
the conclusion returns to the paired scenarios: Answer the motivating question by comparing the mixed-fleet and pure-CV worlds, while retaining country-specific timing and source defects.

unresolved_questions: The source has no title page or Summary/Abstract; physical page 1 is Contents and the paper-internal title is absent.
The task statement is unavailable, so scope and deliverables are reconstructed only from paper-implied framing.
Representative CV, EV, HEV modes and France, USA, China are proxies, not a heterogeneous world sample.
Table 2 historical quantities and Table 3 logistic ceilings are not accompanied by source provenance or fit diagnostics.
The logistic ceiling M and common r=0.115 are asserted without carrying-capacity evidence, residuals, or uncertainty.
The prose says EA rather than EV in the allocation discussion, and the 90% reduction target is a policy premise rather than a reserve inference.
The fleet-allocation block uses eta as an oil-reliance coefficient but the text later says R(t) is both decreasing and rising; symbols and monotonicity are unresolved.
The HEV description reverses the 8/9 oil-only and 1/9 electric-only fractions in different passages; a=50 km and b=420 km also conflict with that ratio.
E, S, B, I and O,H,C,DeltaP have no common scale, units, normalization, or operational definitions, so the objective and bounds cannot be replayed.
Initial EV/HEV share is estimated as 5% from dated projections without a country-specific calibration or uncertainty interval.
Electricity demand uses annual travel and kJ/km while the source does not document year, power, charging loss, or fleet heterogeneity conversions.
The 27.3% off-peak share is read from one stylized daily diagram and treated as constant across countries and years.
Negative China vacancy is interpreted as surplus support, but the model has no nonnegative residual constraint or temporal power limit.
Energy objective units mix cost per kWh or kJ with x_i generation and k_i capacities; currencies, dates, losses, and spatial scope are not frozen.
The thermal share cap is imposed as 10% based on a France comparison, without reliability, reserve, transmission, or transition constraints.
Plant heterogeneity is degraded to E0=10,000,000 kWh per year; a five-year construction circle is not a validated build schedule.
CO2 intensity is a grid-use proxy, not lifecycle emissions; upstream extraction, battery production, transmission, and plant construction are excluded.
The source uses v3-prime, v3, a and b inconsistently, and the HEV oil/electric distance labels are reversed in the numeric paragraph.
Tables 8-9 use 1jk and gCO2/km labels with unclear units, fixed factors, and no uncertainty or sensitivity.
The US and China emissions rises during transition are retained, but the mechanism attribution is internal and not compared with observed series.
Oil saving coefficients C_i and the all-CV counterfactual are not fully defined by vehicle type, distance, fuel, or time units.
World weights r1=2.6462, r2=2.4333, r3=12.1333 are unexplained, not normalized, and extrapolate three countries to the world.
The claim of 2.5 billion L saved in 2055 needs a scale and arithmetic audit against Figure 18.
Driving-cost inputs include an implausible USA electricity price of 6 dollars/kWh and mixed currencies without a common price year.
Maintenance saving is inferred from a linear parts-to-fee relation and one web source; vehicle age, repair mix, and reliability are omitted.
Job and charging-station counts use estimated coefficients and unclear capacity/time units; no displacement, wage, or service-demand model is supplied.
The paper claims jobs near 10% of current population without denominator, labor-market displacement, or uncertainty checks.
Government investment mixes plant, station, subsidy, salary, and currency terms; subsidies are not linked to authority or policy timing.
Output is called monetary reward but adds salary and driving savings without discounting, opportunity cost, taxes, or double-counting controls; prose defines R(t) while formula defines Output(t).
Nitrogen is used as a health proxy but is conflated with nitrogen species and NOx/nitrate/nitrite; the 0.685 ratio is not a health exposure model.
The world synthesis reuses France, USA, and China curves without population, fleet, electricity, or income coverage diagnostics.
The conclusion contains a duplicated China label: 2.42% is assigned to China, 16.2% to USA, and 18.1% is again said to be China.
No uncertainty, sensitivity, held-out validation, lifecycle boundary, or decision-stability analysis supports the assertive global conclusion.
References, URLs, table cells, chart labels, formula-only blocks, headers, and copied citations are excluded from positive language evidence.

writing_logic.summary: global fleet and emissions pressure -> 50-year three-country scope -> CV/EV/HEV classes -> four impact dimensions
fleet quantities -> electricity demand and supply -> environmental/economic/social/health impacts
representative countries and vehicle modes -> explicit simplifications -> downstream data reuse
population/road capacity limits -> biota analogy -> logistic total-fleet equation -> fitted country ceilings
exact reserve date impossible -> reasons stated -> 90% oil-reduction target -> type-allocation equation
total fleet output -> CV/EV/HEV split -> multi-benefit government optimization -> country mix figures
daily load fluctuation -> off-peak surplus -> 27.3% usable share -> residual demand C(t)
off-peak insufficiency -> source options and constraints -> minimum-cost mix -> country mechanisms
plant types/scales impossible to count -> average E0 proxy -> plant count -> construction timing
EV upstream-fossil objection -> grid CO2 intensity -> type emissions -> country transition curves
unfavorable US/China early emissions -> competing fleet/grid mechanisms -> later decline -> bounded benefit
mixed fleet vs all-CV -> country oil savings -> weighted world proxy -> Figure 18
environmental benefit alone insufficient -> individual cost, jobs, investment, and health feasibility metrics
fleet/plant outputs -> station and job equations -> social interpretation -> investment handoff
investment already in money -> jobs and driving savings converted to money -> output/input comparison
CO2-to-nitrogen proxy -> country health curves -> four-impact world scenario comparison
motivating question -> country-specific timing -> individual appeal -> government support -> global close
